text: The dusk came soft. A gentle mist rolled in.
Sunny wandered where the tall ferns brushed the path.
Beside the ferns she heard a quiet sound,
a soft small rustle in the fronds nearby.
A little pademelon, round and shy,
with reddish fur and big dark gentle eyes.
He nibbled softly at the tender grass,
his small ears turning at each tiny sound.
“Hello,” said Sunny, soft so not to fright.
“Hello,” he whispered. “Isn't evening nice?”
He gave a little hop into the ferns,
then peeped back out with soft and shining eyes.
“I love the ferny edge when day is done,” he said,
“all misty-quiet, safe, and cool, and green.”
So Sunny watched the mist drift through the trees,
and saw the first stars twinkle up above.
The pademelon gave a gentle yawn,
his little paws tucked soft against his chest.
He nestled in a hollow lined with fern,
all snug and warm beneath the misty leaves.
Sunny found a bed of moss and fern,
soft and cool and green beneath the trees.
The gully hushed. The mist hung soft and still.
Everything was peaceful, cool, and calm.
Her eyes grew heavy in the gentle mist.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the sleeping pademelon,
safe and snug among the quiet ferns.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little pademelon.
Goodnight, sleepy ferns. Goodnight, little one.
